title: High-value and commercial crops give Gujarat an advantage, while staple yields still trail stronger-performing crop systems
subtitle: Gujarat’s stronger performance in commercial crops sits alongside lower-yield staple systems, creating a two-track productivity agenda across value and food crops.

chart.annotation: Commercial crops lead the yield ranking, while staple crops cluster lower and keep the productivity agenda open.

insights.text: **Cotton** ranks first at **78**, followed by **Groundnut** at **72** and **Castor** at **69**, showing Gujarat’s strength in commercial crop systems.
Staple crops sit lower in the ranking: **Wheat** at **61**, **Rice** at **58**, and **Bajra** at **52**.
The spread from **78** at the top to **52** at the bottom shows that value-crop advantage and staple-system yield improvement both matter in Gujarat.
